findings.detail:
Important, below Critical; reported under the explicit verdict-classification stop. The Bash fallback searches both streams for both verdict kinds, although the documented protocol assigns success summaries to stdout and failure summaries to stderr. For a complete exit-0 result with stdout 'one check ran: OK
unknown final status
' and stderr 'PASS: nested diagnostic
', matches accepts the existing fixture's green expectation despite the unrecognized final stdout summary. Conversely, stderr ending in 'FAIL: nested diagnostic' rejects a valid terminal stdout success. Wrong-stream nested output therefore still controls verdicts.
findings.evidence: framework_summary iterates stderr before stdout at line 144 and accepts a stderr PASS for exit zero at lines 149-153 without examining stdout. matches then finds the required earlier stdout marker in the full capture at line 162. tests/checked_plant_test.py supplies the corresponding green expectation with contains=['one check ran: OK'] and excludes=['SKIP', 'ERROR']. The shared parser governs baseline, control, restored checks and render-time verification. checked-runner.md explicitly assigns Bash success summaries to stdout and failure summaries to stderr. This is a source trace; no reproduction was executed.
findings.title: Parallel paths: Bash verdicts still accept the wrong result stream
